clue.text: Polite poet of the Yukon among those paid from the public purse

definitions.text: those paid from the public purse

parts.note: polite and civil are synonyms, both meaning courteous
Robert Service wrote ballads of the Klondike gold rush in Canada's Yukon

explanation.surface: A courteous Yukon versifier turns out to be on the state payroll.
explanation.definitionFit: Government employees make up the body of officials salaried by the state from taxation.

clue.text: I crave a preparation of luxury food

indicators.note: a preparation is something mixed or made up, so the letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone confesses a longing for an expensive delicacy.
explanation.walkthrough: CAVIARE is an older spelling of caviar.
explanation.definitionFit: Sturgeon roe is the classic expensive delicacy, served as a costly treat.

clue.text: Faces half a dozen wise men

parts.note: six, written as the Roman numeral VI
sages are wise men

explanation.surface: Six wise men confront something together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Faces' looks like a verb, but it is a plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A visage is a literary word for a person's countenance.

clue.text: Most modern aesthetic creation typical of the opsimath

parts.note: the most modern thing is the latest
art is creative work made for its beauty

explanation.surface: A remark about the newest artistic work is linked to someone who learns in old age.
explanation.walkthrough: An opsimath is a person who begins learning late in life.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who takes up study in old age begins later than usual, which is the hallmark of such a learner.

clue.text: To follow in green suede

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the words green suede, running across the gap

explanation.surface: Instructions to come after something while wearing green suede.
explanation.definitionFit: To come after or result from something is the sense here.

clue.text: When it comes to the point a beard is artistic

definitions.text: When it comes to the point a beard

explanation.surface: A pointed beard is said to make a man look like a painter.
explanation.walkthrough: The Flemish painter Anthony van Dyck gave his name to the neat pointed beard seen in his portraits.
explanation.definitionFit: The trimmed pointed beard is named after a Flemish portraitist, and in the painter sense the word names an artist of note.

clue.text: The girl who broke up a circle

indicators.note: breaking something up scatters its parts, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A young woman disbanded a social group.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's given name, so a girl in crossword terms.

clue.text: Current equipment to deal with pressing problems

definitions.text: Current equipment to deal with pressing problems

parts.words: Current equipment to deal with pressing problems
parts.note: current is electricity, and pressing problems are creases that need to be pressed out of clothes

explanation.surface: Up-to-date tools are offered for urgent difficulties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' reads as 'present-day' and 'pressing' as 'urgent', but they mean electric current and ironing.
explanation.definitionFit: A household appliance powered by mains electricity smooths wrinkles from laundry.

clue.text: Contest in which court verdict awards no points to losers

definitions.text: Contest in which court verdict awards no points to losers

parts.words: Contest in which court verdict awards no points to losers
parts.note: court is a tennis court, and a set where the losers win no games at all is won six to nil

explanation.surface: A legal ruling leaves the losing side with nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: In tennis, love means zero, so a set won six games to nil has this name.
explanation.definitionFit: A tennis set in which one player wins every game and the opponent scores nil.

clue.text: Warm well-being for a tanner.

parts.note: warm well-being suggests basking, and a tanner is someone tanning the skin, so this is a session soaking up rays

explanation.surface: Comfort is promised for someone who tans leather.
explanation.walkthrough: A tanner here is a person getting a tan, not a leather worker (nor the old British sixpence, also called a tanner).
explanation.definitionFit: Lying out to bask in sunshine gives the warmth and pleasure a sunbather seeks.

clue.text: His fall set an impossible task for the royal stables and male staff

definitions.text: His fall set an impossible task for the royal stables and male staff

parts.words: His fall set an impossible task for the royal stables and male staff
parts.note: the nursery rhyme says all the king's horses and all the king's men could not put him together again

explanation.surface: A man's downfall leaves the palace grooms and servants with an impossible job.
explanation.walkthrough: The royal stables and male staff are the king's horses and the king's men of the nursery rhyme about the egg who fell off a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: The egg-shaped figure of the nursery rhyme sat on a wall, had a great fall, and could not be mended.

clue.text: Substitutes for campanologists' programmes

explanation.surface: Replacements are offered for the bell-ringers' schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: Campanologists are bell-ringers; a change is one sequence in which a set of bells is rung.
explanation.definitionFit: Substitutes are swaps or replacements, and in bell-ringing the term names the ordered sequences rung on a peal of bells.

clue.text: A fenland city's one hesitation in Paradise

parts.note: Ely is a small cathedral city in the Fens of eastern England
one is the Roman numeral I
um is the sound of someone hesitating

explanation.surface: A small cathedral town's moment of doubt occurs in heaven.
explanation.walkthrough: The Fens are flat marshland in eastern England, where Ely stands.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the Elysian Fields were the blessed afterlife of heroes.

clue.text: Quarter surrounded by Marxists in the wood-wind section

indicators.note: the quarter's letter is placed inside the word for Marxists

parts.note: reds is a common name for communists
E, East, is one quarter of the compass

explanation.surface: A district is ringed by revolutionaries in an orchestra's woodwind.
explanation.definitionFit: Oboes, clarinets and bassoons sound through vibrating reeds, so the players of these instruments are known by that name.

clue.text: Humiliation of a low type of dwelling

parts.note: a basement is a home below ground level

explanation.surface: Being forced to live underground is a humbling experience.
explanation.definitionFit: Being degraded or brought low in esteem is shame and humbling.

clue.text: Starch producing plant put to use by the Archers?

definitions.text: Starch producing plant put to use by the Archers?

parts.words: Starch producing plant put to use by the Archers?
parts.note: archers use arrows, and the plant's starchy root shares the name of what they shoot

explanation.surface: A starchy crop is grown by the family in a radio soap.
explanation.walkthrough: The Archers is a long-running BBC radio soap about a farming family, so the surface suggests a farm crop.
explanation.definitionFit: A tropical plant whose tuber yields a fine starch used in cooking.

clue.text: Craftsman to find fault and come in

parts.note: to carp is to complain pettily
to enter is to come in

explanation.surface: A tradesman arrives and starts grumbling.
explanation.definitionFit: A woodworker is a skilled tradesman.

clue.text: Otherwise turning to madness in S.E. Europe

indicators.note: turning around means the word for otherwise is read backwards

parts.note: or introduces an alternative, meaning otherwise
mania is a form of madness

explanation.surface: Another option is to go mad in the Balkans.
explanation.definitionFit: The country lies on the Black Sea in the south-east of the continent.

clue.text: Neat oil blended for high spirits

indicators.note: blending mixes things, so the letters are combined in a new order

explanation.surface: Undiluted oil is mixed to lift the mood.
explanation.definitionFit: Joy and exhilaration are a lift in mood.

clue.text: The bike that fretted

explanation.surface: A bicycle is said to have worried.
explanation.definitionFit: A small motor-assisted bicycle, and the past tense of a verb meaning to sulk or brood listlessly.

clue.text: More about to speak falsely for the author of Tartuffe

indicators.note: about means going round, so the word More is wrapped around the word for lying

parts.note: to lie is to speak falsely

explanation.surface: Extra dishonesty is attributed to a French playwright.
explanation.definitionFit: Tartuffe is a seventeenth-century French comedy about a religious hypocrite, by the dramatist Jean-Baptiste Poquelin.

clue.text: Persian fairy having a tendency to personal charm

parts.note: a peri is a fairy or sprite in Persian mythology
apt means inclined or likely to do something

explanation.surface: A Persian sprite is naturally inclined to be personally attractive.
explanation.definitionFit: An amulet worn on the body against harm is a charm in the talisman sense.

clue.text: Violent behaviour of the swindle era

parts.note: a ramp is old British slang for a racket or swindle
an age is an era

explanation.surface: A period of fraud is marked by violence.
explanation.definitionFit: Running amok is wild, destructive conduct.

clue.text: Nigel transmogrified as the Lord of Marbles

indicators.note: transmogrified means changed in form, so the letters of Nigel are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man called Nigel is transformed into a nobleman with a collection.
explanation.walkthrough: The seventh Earl of Elgin brought sculptures from the Parthenon to Britain, still known as the Elgin Marbles.
explanation.definitionFit: The Earl who removed the Parthenon sculptures gave his title to them.

clue.text: Predator joins leader of the flock to produce valuable ore

parts.note: a wolf is a predatory animal
a ram is the male sheep that leads the flock

explanation.surface: A hunter attacks the head sheep for profit.
explanation.definitionFit: The German-derived name for tungsten, and for its mineral source wolframite.

clue.text: Chinese city ruler follows Ann in confusion

indicators.note: follows means the word for ruler comes after the jumbled name
confusion jumbles things, so the letters of Ann are rearranged

parts.note: a king is a ruler

explanation.surface: A monarch walks behind a flustered woman called Ann.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Follows' puts the ruler after the jumbled name; the city is now usually written Nanjing.
explanation.definitionFit: The old romanised name of Nanjing, on the Yangtze in China.

clue.text: Put on a hammy performance as a covert alternative

indicators.note: an alternative form of the letters is another arrangement of them

explanation.surface: Someone advises ham acting as an option to secret action.
explanation.definitionFit: To exaggerate a role on stage is to ham it up.

clue.text: Source of reports for the City pages?

definitions.text: Source of reports for the City pages?

parts.words: Source of reports for the City pages?
parts.note: reports are the bangs of guns firing, and the City is the financial district of London where this road runs

explanation.surface: A newspaper's financial section is seeking its news source.
explanation.walkthrough: The City is London's financial district, home of a mainline station and street named for a cannon; 'reports' are bangs, not news stories.
explanation.definitionFit: A street and railway station in the City of London whose name contains a big gun, which makes reports.
